     def __getitem__(self, key: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
         raise NotImplementedError()  # pragma: no cover
+
+
+class SQLAlchemyRecord(Record):
+    """Record wrapper around a SQLAlchemy :class:`~sqlalchemy.engine.Row`.
+
+    SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed the mapping style access (``row["key"]`` and
+    ``dict(row)`` support) from :class:`~sqlalchemy.engine.Row`.  The
+    ``databases`` Record interface however is documented as supporting this
+    behaviour, so we wrap the underlying SQLAlchemy row in this class which
+    restores it while continuing to delegate all other behaviour to the row.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_row",)
+
+    def __init__(self, row: typing.Any) -> None:
+        self._row = row
+
+    @property
+    def _mapping(self) -> typing.Mapping:
+        return self._row._mapping
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
+        if isinstance(key, int):
+            return self._row[key]
+        return self._row._mapping[key]
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> typing.Iterator:
+        return iter(self._row)
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._row)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> typing.Any:
+        return getattr(self._row, name)
+
+    def keys(self) -> typing.KeysView:
+        return self._mapping.keys()
+
+    def values(self) -> typing.ValuesView:
+        return self._mapping.values()
+
+    def items(self) -> typing.ItemsView:
+        return self._mapping.items()

## Summary of changes

The SQLAlchemy dependency was upgraded from 1.4 to 2.0.52, which removed several APIs the `databases` library relied on. I fixed the source to work with the new version:

### 1. `Row` constructor changed in SQLAlchemy 2.0
SQLAlchemy 2.0's `Row` no longer accepts the 4th `key_style` positional argument and expects `key_to_index` instead of the raw `keymap`:

- `databases/backends/sqlite.py`, `mysql.py`, `aiopg.py`, `asyncmy.py`
- Changed every `Row(...)` construction from the 1.4 form
  `Row(metadata, metadata._processors, metadata._keymap, Row._default_key_style, row)`
  to the 2.0 form
  `Row(metadata, metadata._effective_processors, metadata._key_to_index, row)`.

### 2. `Row` no longer supports mapping-style access in SQLAlchemy 2.0
SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed `row["col"]`, `dict(row)` and `row.keys()` from `Row`, which the `databases` `Record` interface exposes. I added a wrapper that restores that contract while delegating to the underlying row:

- `databases/interfaces.py` — added `SQLAlchemyRecord(Record)`; it supports integer indexing/iteration/`len` via the row, key access (strings and `Column` objects) via `row._mapping`, attribute access, and re-exposes `keys()`/`values()`/`items()` so `dict(record)` works.
- The four backends above now wrap every returned row in `SQLAlchemyRecord`.

### 3. Tests that called the removed list-form `select([...])`
Per the rules, I updated only the failing call sites in `tests/test_databases.py` where tests used the SQLAlchemy API removed in 2.0 (`select([...])`), changing them to the positional form (`select(notes.c.text)`, `select(notes.c.id, notes.c.text)`, `select(articles, custom_date)`).
